faq: Which Squarespace template should I use?

Tell us your business and the style you like, and we choose a starting layout that fits. Since Squarespace 7.1 templates share the same editing tools, the look can be changed later without starting over.
Do you need my Squarespace password?
No. You invite us as a contributor from your site's permissions settings. We never ask for your password and you can remove us when the work is done.
Who pays for the Squarespace plan and domain?
You do, directly to Squarespace. A Business or Commerce plan is needed to sell products. We build on a trial where possible and you choose a plan when you are ready to publish.
Can you set up payments for the shop?
Yes. We connect Stripe, PayPal or Squarespace Payments, plus shipping and tax settings, in your account. The payment provider's own sign-up and identity checks stay with you.
desc:
A Squarespace site build for your brand starts from the template that suits your business and ends with pages, forms and a small shop ready to launch. Ecom Swift LLC builds it in your own account and shows you how to edit it afterward.

## What is a Squarespace site build?

A Squarespace site build is the creation of a complete website inside a Squarespace account, from the first template choice to a launch checklist. It includes your branding, page layouts, contact form, newsletter sign-up and, if you sell, a shop with products and checkout.

You own the site from day one because it is created in your account and not on ours.

## Why a planned build beats starting alone

Many owners begin a site on their own, add pages as ideas come and end up with an uneven result. The menu has too many items, headings use different sizes and the phone view was never checked. Fixing a site later takes more time than planning it at the start.

A build begins with structure: which pages exist, what each one should achieve and where visitors should go next. Design comes after structure, so the look supports the message.

## How the build shapes enquiries and sales

A clear site helps people act. A visitor who lands on a page should see what you offer, who you serve and how to contact you without scrolling through filler. A connected contact form means enquiries reach your inbox, and a newsletter sign-up lets interested visitors stay in touch.

For shops, product pages, categories and checkout settings affect whether browsing turns into a purchase. Titles and descriptions help the pages appear in search, and a mobile review catches problems before customers meet them.

## What a well-built Squarespace site includes

- A template chosen to match your type of business.
- Your logo, fonts and colors applied through site styles.
- Pages laid out with Fluid Engine and consistent spacing.
- A contact form that delivers to your inbox.
- A newsletter sign-up connected to your email tool.
- Page titles and descriptions written for each page.
- Google Analytics connected, so you can see visits.
- A shop with products, options and payment settings.
- A blog with starter posts, in the larger package.
- A mobile check and a launch checklist.

## How we build it

We discuss your business, pick the template and plan the page list. We then apply your branding, write the layouts and connect the forms. If you want to sell, we create the shop and add products. Before launch we review speed and the phone layout, and we connect your domain when you approve.

The Basic package builds a tidy brand site with a few pages. Standard adds more pages, a small shop, a newsletter and analytics. Premium delivers a complete site with a shop, blog, light code styling, a final review and an editing walkthrough, followed by a period of fixes.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Prepare your logo, photos and main text before the build starts.
- Decide the goal of each page.
- Keep the menu short.
- Plan who will update the site after launch.

**Avoid:**
- Choosing a template only for its demo photos.
- Adding many pages with little to say.
- Mixing a long list of typefaces on one site.
- Launching without a test enquiry and a test order.

## Who this is for

A new consultant needs a credible presence before the first client call. A craft business wants a small shop with a newsletter. An established company with only a social page wants its own site under its own domain.

## What we need from you

Send a short brief, your logo and any text and images you have. We never need passwords. Create the Squarespace account yourself, so the plan and domain stay in your name, then invite us as a contributor. If you want payments in the shop, you connect your own payment provider account and we guide you through the settings.
